title: Heuristics playbook: evals triage notes
content:
Context and purpose:
- Personal prep + lightweight playbook for the upcoming Optimize / Evals triage session (weekly).
- Focus: recent quality regression flagged by monitoring (delta in BLEU-like and human-sim metrics on prompt set B), plus noisy A/B where variant v2 sometimes improves cost but hurts hallucination rate.
- Goal: leave meeting with 3 prioritized, owner-assigned experiments and a short rollback/hard-guard plan if customer-facing metrics degrade further.

Quick TL;DR (to read in <2 min):
- What we see: A/B on routing->v2 shows -12% token cost (win) but +8% hallucination rate on enterprise prompt set (regression). Heatmap shows failures concentrated on prompts with long context + named-entity recall.
- Primary hypothesis: v2 uses a different decoder temperature decay (aggressive pruning) + new token-filtering kernel; this reduces low-prob tokens (cost) but slightly biases generation away from factual recall.
- Quick triage wins: run focused evals on 200 promptrs with entity masking; reproduce on local quantized variant; test simple prompt template fallback in routing.

Data snapshot (what to show in meeting):
- A/B cohort sizes: control 11.2k requests, v2 10.9k requests (last 48h).
- Observed deltas: token-cost per request -12%; time-to-first-byte unchanged; hallucination proxy (entity-bleu) +8% regression; subjective quality score (crowd) -0.3/5 on subset.
- Heatmap notes: failures cluster where: long context > 1.2k tokens OR question requires multi-step synthesis (list of steps).
- Quick reproduction: running eval-scripts locally on the nightly v2 image reproduces +4% entity-bleu delta on 2k examples (smaller magnitude but same sign).

Hypothesis ranking (1=most likely):
1) Decoding heuristic change (temperature decay / nucleus sampling tweak) reduces exploration needed for factual recall -> increases hallucinations.
2) Token-filtering kernel (new quantized kernel) introduces distributional bias on rare tokens (names/entities).
3) Batching / KV cache behavior in v2 affects cross-request cache invalidation for long contexts -> occasional missing context.
4) Data/finetune mismatch: v2 was validated on shorter prompt distributions; edge cases were underweighted.

Immediate experiments (fast, low-cost, 48–72h):
- EXP-A (priority 1): Re-run v2 with control's decoding schedule on a 2k-sample subset (owner: Kenji). Purpose: isolate decoding as cause. Output: compare token histograms, top-k distribution, and entity-bleu.
- EXP-B (priority 2): Swap v2 kernel for previous token-filter implementation on a small dedicated pool (owner: Priya). Purpose: test kernel bias.
- EXP-C (priority 3): Add a routing rule: if prompt length > 1k AND prompt contains >3 named entities, route to control model (owner: me / Amelia). Purpose: quick mitigation fallback.

Prompt-set dive (notes and candidate changes):
- Problematic examples appear to follow two patterns: 1) multi-step synthesis w/ long chains of facts; 2) heavy named-entity recall (legal text, customer lists).
- Candidate prompt templates to test:
  * instructive-priming: explicitly ask model to \"quote verbatim\" or \"refer to source: <context>\" before generation. Hypothesis: reduces freeform hallucination.
  * constrained-generation: limit answer to enumerated bullets and require citation tokens.
- Quick change to try in canary: append explicit anchor token \"<SOURCE-ANCHOR>\" before the final question (owner: Quentin).
- Note: need to be careful with customer-facing templates — do not modify for existing customers without opt-in. Use canary routing.

A/B analysis specifics (what to compute during meeting):
- Per-prompt paired comparison where possible (same prompt sent to both variants). Use McNemar-style test for binary hallucination label.
- Token-level KL / JS divergence between control and v2 distributions on problem prompts.
- Confidence bands: bootstrap with 10k resamples on the 2k-sample reproduction set.

Escalation / rollback criteria (proposed):
- Immediate rollback to control if enterprise prompt set hallucination proxy increases >5% relative and sustained over 2 consecutive 12h windows.
- Soft guard: disable v2 routing for accounts with >20% of requests classified as \"sensitive\" (legal/medical) until mitigations validated.

Meeting agenda (30–40 min):
1) 5m: Quick data readout (Kenji) — top-line deltas + heatmap.
2) 8m: Reproduction status (Amelia) — local repro numbers and assumptions.
3) 10m: Hypotheses + experiment plan (open) — agree owners/priorities.
4) 7m: Short mitigation decision (routing/rollback) — decide immediate action.
5) 5m: Parking lot, next steps, who writes follow-up.

Notes on instrumentation / quick checks to run now (before meeting):
- Produce per-request top-5 token distributions for 100 failing prompts (script: eval-scripts/topk-hist.py). Attach to PR.
- Run entity detection overlay to verify whether named entities are being truncated / miss-encoded during tokenization.
- Confirm kv-cache consistency logs for long-context requests in v2 (SRE: check INF-1298).

Open questions / uncertainties (call these out):
- Is there any difference in pre-processing between control and v2 CI (tokenization flags, normalizers)? Need to confirm.
- How much of the delta comes from a small fraction of "super-fail" prompts vs. a broad shift? (run Pareto analysis).
- Crowd label variance: do we trust the subjective crowd delta (-0.3) or is it within annotator noise?

Decisions to make by EOD after triage: who will own each experiment; whether to flip routing rule for affected enterprise accounts; and whether to cut a hotfix release for kernel if bias confirmed.

Follow-up action items (assignments):
- Kenji: run EXP-A, deliver comparison histograms + statistical test by 2026-03-07. Update INF ticket.
- Priya: stand up small pool to swap token-filter kernel (EXP-B), collect 24h metrics and logs by 2026-03-08.
- Quentin: implement routing rule proof-of-concept (EXP-C) in canary and smoke test by 2026-03-06.
- Amelia (me): coordinate reproductions, assemble one-pager with top 10 failing prompts and attach to PR; draft rollback language for CS by 2026-03-06.
- SRE on-call (ping via INF-1298): export kv-cache traces for 10 long-context failures and share by 2026-03-06.

Parking lot (things not for this triage):
- Full retrain or tuning of whole model family (scope too large).
- Changing pricing/billing or rate limits — out of scope.
- UX-level template changes for customers — needs PM sign-off.

Quick links for meeting deck (short):
- Repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/tree/main/repro
- PR with topk hist tool: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/pull/256
- INF ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-1298

Notes to self (scratchy):
- If decoding change is confirmed, consider a middle ground: keep cost kernels but fall back to control decoding for prompts with >X entities.
- Watch out for metrics double-counting (token-cost population vs. routed population).
- Keep language minimal for CS: "we're rolling small mitigation while we verify root cause" — avoid technical detail in external comms.
summary: Notes and playbook-style triage for Optimize/evals meeting: reproduce regression, prioritize decoding vs. kernel hypothesis, 3 quick experiments (swap decoding schedule, swap kernel, routing fallback), and clear escalation thresholds.
